title: RUSSIAN COSMONAUTS CONDUCT SPACEWALK TO ACTIVATE NEW STATION ROBOTIC ARM
description: Expedition 67 cosmonauts Oleg Artemyev and Denis Matveev conducted the first in a series of spacewalks April 18 outside the International Space Station to install a control panel for a new European robotic arm attached to the Nauka Multipurpose Laboratory Module and activate the arm. The European robotic arm launched on Nauka, and will be used to move payloads and spacewalkers around the Russian segment of the complex.  Get the latest from NASA delivered every week. via: the NASA Image and Video Library

transcript.text: Russian spacewalk. 52 will be conducted by Oleg Artimyev, EV-1 in the red stripes
and Denis Matveev, EV-2 in the blue stripes.
To start the spacewalk the crew will egress Poisk with a crew lock bag
and the EMMI, also known as the
the European Robotic Arm EVA Control Panel or ERA EVA control panel.
After turning on their cameras and lights, both crew will start translating down
the Strela booms from Poisk to the NAUKA module
where they'll begin their work site setup.
EV-2 will install a pallet adapter on handrail 4401 and the crew will work
together to structurally secure the EMMI.
Oleg and Denis will then mate the CBT Cable
and power on the EMMI for check out.
While Oleg works the EMMI check out,
Denis will translate to the base point worksite where he'll remove
a total of four protective covers and take imagery of the interfaces.
After closing up the EMMI covers,
Oleg will translate to the ERA arm where he'll begin folding back
the MLI blanket to install one of several ERA arm handrail
Denis will translate over to the ERA arm
where he'll assist with the handrail installs.
The crew will finish installing
the last handrail near the ERA arm elbow on limb number two.
Oleg will then take photos of the solar reflectors near the elbow.
Oleg and Denis will translate back to Poisk and stow the covers,
as well as the crew lock bag back inside the airlock.
Using the same translation path they did earlier, they'll head back down
to one of the NAUKA's passive payload interfaces.
While working together, they'll install the adapter and remove the manual drive.
EV-1 anbd EV-2 will translate back to the airlock, stow the manual drive.
Afterwards, they'll perform an inventory
and then the ingress close the hatch, finishing out Russian spacewalk 52.
